notes.meaning: Give generously to those in need, even when it feels like your gift is lost like bread thrown into the water. God promises that kindness shown to others will come back to you in due time. Giving freely without demanding immediate results is the heart of true generosity.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars see this as an image of maritime trade, where merchants sent grain across the sea and waited patiently for the ships to return with profit.

notes.meaning: Share what you have with many different people, giving to seven or even eight. Troubles and hard times can strike the land without warning, leaving anyone in need. Generosity now helps others and prepares a circle of support before disaster arrives.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church teachers such as Gregory the Great interpreted the numbers seven and eight spiritually, taking seven as this earthly life and eight as the resurrection, urging believers to share earthly goods while keeping eternal life in view.

notes.meaning: Certain events in nature happen according to fixed laws that people cannot change. Full clouds will pour down rain, and a fallen tree will lie wherever the storm blew it down. Because life brings sudden and unchangeable troubles, people should do good while they still have the opportunity.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian writers such as Jerome applied the fallen tree to a person at death, teaching that a soul's final state in heaven or hell is fixed once earthly life ends.

notes.meaning: A farmer who constantly watches the wind will never plant, and one who keeps staring at the clouds will never reap a harvest. Waiting for ideal conditions causes people to miss their chance to work. We must move forward with our duties instead of letting uncertainty paralyze us.

No one can trace the path of the wind or explain how bones grow in a mother's womb. In the same way, human beings cannot understand the hidden work of God, who created everything. Since God's plans are beyond our grasp, we must trust Him and faithfully do our daily work.

Plant your seed early in the morning and keep working until the evening arrives. No one knows which effort will succeed, or whether both will bring a good yield. Diligent and steady labor is our responsibility, while the final outcome rests with God.

Natural light is pleasant, and seeing the sun brings joy to human eyes. Here, light stands for the gift of life itself, which is sweet and worth cherishing. People ought to welcome each day with gratitude as a good gift from God.

If a person lives through many years, they should enjoy the good in all of them. Yet they must also keep in mind that the dark days of old age and the grave will be many. Life on earth passes quickly, so we should live each day with eternity in mind.

Young people are encouraged to enjoy their energy and find gladness in the days of their youth. They may pursue their desires, but they must remember that God will bring every action into judgment. True joy is found when youthfulness is paired with a healthy respect for God's holy law.

Remove sorrow, anger, and troubling passions from your heart, and turn away from things that bring harm to your body. Youth and strength pass by quickly, disappearing like a shadow. Turning from evil in our younger years spares us from deep regrets later on.
